title: Neural network-driven domain decomposition for efficient solutions to the Helmholtz equation
abstract: arXiv:2511.15445v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Accurately simulating wave propagation is crucial in fields such as acoustics, electromagnetism, and seismic analysis. Traditional numerical methods, like finite difference and finite element approaches, are widely used to solve governing partial differential equations (PDEs) such as the Helmholtz equation. However, these methods face significant computational challenges when applied to high-frequency wave problems in complex two-dimensional domains. This work investigates Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks (FBPINNs) and their multilevel extensions as a promising alternative. These methods leverage domain decomposition, partitioning the computational domain into overlapping sub-domains, each governed by a local neural network. translated_title: 神经网络驱动的区域分解方法用于高效求解亥姆霍兹方程
translated_abstract: 精确模拟波传播在声学、电磁学和地震分析等领域至关重要。传统的数值方法，如有限差分法和有限元法，被广泛用于求解亥姆霍兹方程等控制性偏微分方程（PDE）。然而，当应用于复杂二维区域中的高频波问题时，这些方法面临显著的计算挑战。本研究探讨了有限基物理信息神经网络（FBPINNs）及其多层级扩展作为一种有前景的替代方案。这些方法利用区域分解技术，将计算域划分为相互重叠的子区域，每个子区域由一个局部神经网络负责。我们评估了这些方法在求解齐次情形下亥姆霍兹方程时的精度和计算效率，展示了它们缓解传统方法局限性的潜力。
tldr: 本研究利用有限基物理信息神经网络（FBPINNs）及其多层级扩展，通过将计算域分解为重叠子区域的区域分解策略，高效求解复杂二维域中的高频亥姆霍兹方程，克服了传统数值方法的计算瓶颈。
en_tdlr: This work leverages Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks (FBPINNs) and their multilevel extensions with domain decomposition to efficiently solve high-frequency Helmholtz equations in complex 2D domains, overcoming the computational limitations of traditional numerical methods.
